extraction.name: LUMA
extraction.description: A multimodal benchmark dataset with audio, image, and text modalities designed for learning from uncertain data, with tools to inject varying types and degrees of uncertainty.

extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was compiled from multiple sources: images from CIFAR-10/100, audio extracted and validated from The Spoken Wikipedia, LibriSpeech, Mozilla Common Voice, plus some voluntary contributions, and text generated with Gemma-7B Instruct based on class labels.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Software Collection, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images were sourced from CIFAR-10/100; audio from The Spoken Wikipedia, LibriSpeech, Mozilla Common Voice, and 73 colleague-contributed recordings; text was generated using Gemma-7B Instruct.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset package supports controlled manipulation by adjusting data diversity, adding modality-specific sample noise, injecting label noise, and adding out-of-distribution samples.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Audio samples were extracted from aligned transcripts, automatically validated with Whisper Large V3, manually validated for negative predictions, anonymized and trimmed for colleague contributions, and invalid or conflicting samples were filtered out. Text samples were validated by masking labels and reclassifying with Gemma-7B Instruct.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Manual annotation was used for audio validation. Annotators were shown an audio sample and asked whether it said the target word, with answer options Yes or No. Samples confirmed by both annotators were accepted and conflicting ones were rejected.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper reports annotation agreement and describes how final labels were derived by accepting only samples with agreement from both annotators and rejecting conflicts.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: M.Sc. and PhD students, and professors with advanced to fluent English knowledge
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: OpenAI Whisper Large V3; Gemma-7B Instruct
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to support development of trustworthy and robust machine learning approaches for safety-critical applications.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The generated text modality contains offensive biases and stereotypes, especially gender bias for the classes man, woman, boy, and girl.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The text data may contain factual inaccuracies or biases and should not be used as a source of knowledge or information. The authors also note they cannot assess how accurate or consistent the LLM-based bias detections are.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking multimodal learning algorithms on uncertain data; development, evaluation, and benchmarking of trustworthy and robust multimodal deep learning approaches; training and testing with generated versions containing 500 training and 100 testing samples per class.

isLiveDataset.evidence: In this paper, we propose LUMA, a multimodal dataset for learning from uncertain and multimodal data.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: We compiled the images from the CIFAR 10/100 dataset [18], extracted, validated, and associated audio samples corresponding to the CIFAR image class labels from three diverse audio corpora [2,15,27], and generated the text modality based on the class labels using the Gemma-7B Instruct [25] Large Language Model (LLM).

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: We compiled the images from the CIFAR 10/100 dataset [18], extracted, validated, and associated audio samples corresponding to the CIFAR image class labels from three diverse audio corpora [2,15,27], and generated the text modality based on the class labels using the Gemma-7B Instruct [25] Large Language Model (LLM).

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: For that purpose, we chose CIFAR-100 and CIFAR-10 [18] datasets... For this task, we used three audio/text parallel corpora and extracted the desired audio segments. More specifically, we used The Spoken Wikipedia [15], LibriSpeech [27], and Mozilla Common Voice [2] corpora... we utilized Google’s Gemma-7B Instruct model [25] to generate more than 1,200 texts samples per class

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: We prioritized flexibility, offering multiple options for controlling uncertainty through adjustable parameters such as data diversity, sample-level noise, label corruption, and the injection of out-of-distribution (OOD) samples.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: The automatic validation was achieved with the OpenAI’s Whisper Large V3 model [29] for audio transcription, and transcribed the extracted audio samples. If the transcription corresponded to the class label (or its plural form), then we considered the sample as valid. Otherwise, the sample was sent for manual validation... 73 additional recordings of pronunciations belonging to 4 classes ("roses", "telephone", "whale", "wolf") were voluntarily contributed by our colleagues, which were anonymized, trimmed, and added to the dataset... To validate that the generated texts accurately represent the labels, we masked all label occurrences in the text and fed the masked text back into the Gemma-7B Instruct model

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: For manual validation, we decided to check only the classes, which did not have more than 800 samples... The interface provided the audio sample, with the prompt "Is the audio saying the word below? (An extra ’s’ or ’es’ in the pronunciation is okay.)" and answer options of "Yes" or "No"... We got 71.61% annotation agreement and accepted 5,027 samples, where both annotators confirmed the validity of the sample. Samples with conflicting annotations were rejected.

rai:dataAnnotationPlatform.evidence: We opted for Label Studio [31] to build the labeling interface.

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: In total, we collected 2 annotations per sample, from 17 annotators. We got 71.61% annotation agreement and accepted 5,027 samples, where both annotators confirmed the validity of the sample. Samples with conflicting annotations were rejected.

rai:annotationsPerItem.evidence: In total, we collected 2 annotations per sample, from 17 annotators.

rai:annotatorDemographics.evidence: We asked our colleagues (M.Sc. and PhD students, and professors) with advanced to fluent English knowledge to annotate the samples.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: The automatic validation was achieved with the OpenAI’s Whisper Large V3 model [29] for audio transcription... To validate that the generated texts accurately represent the labels, we masked all label occurrences in the text and fed the masked text back into the Gemma-7B Instruct model

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: We anticipate that the LUMA dataset will help the research community to design more trustworthy and robust machine learning approaches for safety critical applications.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: After manually analyzing some of the generated texts, we noticed that there were samples with offensive biases and stereotypes... Particularly, we noticed a lots of gender bias for classes "man", "woman", "boy" and "girl".

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: Since textual data was generated using an LLM, we recognize that the dataset may contain factual inaccuracies, or biases, but our aim is to offer a benchmark to study uncertainty quantification in multimodal classification settings. LUMA shall not be used as a source of knowledge or information. Although the model identified a high level of bias in these classes, indicating a potential for LLM-based bias detection, we are unable to assess how accurate or consistent these detections truly are.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: To address this challenge, we introduce LUMA (Learning from Uncertain and Multimodal data), a multimodal dataset specifically designed for benchmarking multimodal learning algorithms on uncertain data... This comprehensive dataset and its tools are intended to promote and support the development, evaluation, and benchmarking of trustworthy and robust multimodal deep learning approaches... Each generated version of the dataset consists of 600 data records per class (500 for training, and 100 for testing)
